title: Out of Nowhere, Into the Record Books: Patterson's 168 and Alex Baker's Long Way Back
title_candidates: Out of Nowhere, Into the Record Books: Patterson's 168 and Alex Baker's Long Way Back
No Form, No History, No Problem: Patterson Wins the Trophy with a Record 168
87 and 115: Seve's Last Course Sorts the Field, Patterson Sorts the Trophy
Level at the 14th: Alex Baker's Best Golf Ends Six Short
theme: A TEG of records in both directions on the Lisbon Coast: the man with no TEG history posts the highest Trophy total ever recorded, Mullin sets a course record and his best-ever gross, Alex Baker sets the worst round Royal Óbidos has seen and then plays the golf of his life — and in almost every case the closing five holes did the deciding.
tone: house — faithful, tongue-in-cheek, Ronay/Peck: dry, character-led, every gag anchored to a number the players can check
opening_hook: Open on R4 at Praia D'El Rey, Alex Baker walking off the 14th level with John Patterson for the Trophy lead (b23) — a man who three days earlier had shot the worst round in Royal Óbidos history — then loop back to R1 to explain how either of them got there.
foreshadow: John Patterson arrived with no TEG honours to his name and first visits to both Lisbon Coast courses — a blank page in a field of past champions.
Alex Baker's R1 at Royal Óbidos was 115 gross, the worst round ever recorded there (cr02) — remember it when he is level for the lead on the 14th tee of R4.
At both courses the run home — holes 14 to 18 — kept handing out the tournament: note Neumann bleeding 16 shots there in R1 (b44).
Stuart Neumann came in as reigning Wooden Spoon holder, and his round scores got better every single day: 23, 30, 37, 37.

competitions.name: Trophy (Stableford)
competitions.winner_or_loser: John Patterson (winner, 168 pts, by 6 from Alex Baker)
competitions.how: Patterson opened 38 at Royal Óbidos despite a 10 at the SI-1 4th (b05) and a 7 at the 15th, sitting 2nd, one behind Jon Baker. He took the outright lead at the very first hole of R2 and then posted 49 pts at Praia D'El Rey — the 2nd-best round in TEG history to date (b03) — built on 17 points across holes 9-13 (b06) and 14 more over the last four (b19), turning a one-point deficit into a 10-point cushion. Back at Óbidos in R3 the course bit: quadruple bogeys at the 12th and the 18th (b31, b32) held him to 34 and the lead shrank to 3. In R4 he made a 9 at the SI-2 5th (b17) and Alex Baker drew level on the 14th (b23) — then Baker went 8-7-7 and bled 11 shots over 14-17 (b45) while Patterson closed with 47 for 168 pts, the highest Trophy total in TEG history, and won by 6 (b01). Also his best gross total, +88 (b15).

competitions.name: Green Jacket (Gross)
competitions.winner_or_loser: David Mullin (winner, +67, by 10 from Jon Baker)
competitions.how: Wire-to-wire, and effectively over on the first evening: Mullin's 87 at Royal Óbidos was a new course record, beating the 90 that had stood across six prior visits (cr01), and also his personal best there. He took the outright Gross lead at R1 H18 and was never headed across the remaining 54 holes — lead 2, then 7, 7 and 10. A quintuple-bogey 9 at the 10th in R3 (b16) was the only real wobble and cost him nothing, and +67 is the lowest gross total in TEG history and his own best (b02) — a 7th Jacket, and back-to-back-to-back. Jon Baker was runner-up with a personal-best +77 (b14), Jacket second place for the fourth time in five TEGs, including a new Óbidos personal best of 89 in R1.

competitions.name: Wooden Spoon
competitions.how: Bottom of the Trophy table after every single round, and the floor was laid on day one: 23 pts at Royal Óbidos, with a 9 at the SI-1 4th and the run home from the 14th costing 16 shots (b44) — the 8 at the par-3 15th (b29) dropped him to last outright and he never got off it. From there his golf genuinely improved every round — 30, then 37, then 37, including 16 points across holes 11-15 in R4 (b11) and a new Royal Óbidos personal best of 98 in R3 — but the R1 hole was too deep, and 127 pts made it back-to-back Spoons after TEG 8 (b22). The Praia D'El Rey number stings most: 14 shots worse than his last visit there.

headline_candidates: Level at the 14th, Eleven Shots Later Alex Baker Was Second

Alex Baker Plays the Golf of His Life and Still Finishes Six Back
rounds.chosen_headline: Level at the 14th, Eleven Shots Later Alex Baker Was Second
rounds.angle: The payoff: Baker draws level on the 14th (b23), then bleeds 11 shots over 14-17 (b45) even as he equals his personal-best 44 pts / +27 (b09, b10); Patterson answers a 9 at the SI-2 5th (b17) with 47 pts and a record 168 (b01), Mullin closes out +67 (b02), Williams's escalating one-hole habit reaches an 11 at the 7th (b27), and Neumann's best golf of the tournament still ends in the Spoon (b11, b22).

players.arc: The one man in the field with no TEG history and no previous sight of either course, who survived a 10 at the SI-1 4th on day one (b05), produced the 2nd-best round in TEG history at Praia D'El Rey (b03), rode out a 34 at Óbidos, and closed with 47 for 168 pts — the highest Trophy total ever recorded (b01) — plus a best gross of +88 (b15).

From the worst round in Royal Óbidos history (115 gross, cr02, including an 11 at the 14th, b04) to level for the Trophy lead on the 14th tee of the final round (b23) via two personal-best 44-point rounds (b07, b09) and a personal-best gross total of +127 (b12) — and then 11 shots gone over four closing holes (b45) and a second successive runner-up finish.

Set the Royal Óbidos course record with an 87 in R1 (cr01), led the Gross from the 18th hole of day one to the last, and turned it into +67 — the lowest gross total in TEG history and a 7th Green Jacket (b02) — with a quintuple-bogey 9 at the 10th in R3 (b16) filed as an eccentricity rather than a threat.

Held the Trophy lead after R1 on the back of a nine-shot personal best at Óbidos (89), then watched Patterson disappear over the horizon in R2, and finished Jacket runner-up again — with a personal-best +77 (b14) — for the fourth time in five TEGs; the Baker brothers both finished second at something.

The defending champion posted his best-ever gross total, +115 (b13), and a new Óbidos personal best of 97, while also detonating exactly one hole per round in escalating denominations: 9 at the 15th in R1 (b25), 10 at the 9th in R2 (b26), 11 at the 7th in R4 (b27).

Reigning Spoon holder who lost this one on the very first afternoon — 16 shots gone from the 14th at Óbidos (b44), last outright from the 15th (b29) — and then improved every round (23-30-37-37, b11) without ever climbing off the bottom rung, making it back-to-back Spoons (b22).

venue_notes: TEG's 3rd visit to the Lisbon Coast, October 2016, alternating two courses: Royal Óbidos (R1 the 2nd TEG round there, R3 the 3rd) — Seve Ballesteros' final design, a Challenge Tour championship layout with water in play — and Praia D'El Rey (R2 the 3rd TEG round there, R4 the 4th), parkland out, dunes and links coastline coming home. Use Óbidos as the record-breaker's course (87 and 115 on the same afternoon) and Praia D'El Rey's coastal back nine as the home of the closing-stretch motif: Patterson gained 14 points over 15-18 in R2, Alex Baker lost 11 shots over 14-17 in R4.
course_history_notes: Mullin's 87 in R1 was both a new Royal Óbidos course record (prior best 90 across six visits, cr01) and his own personal best there, three better than TEG 7.

Alex Baker set new personal bests at both courses this TEG — 100 at Praia D'El Rey in R2 (nine better than TEG 7) and 102 at Royal Óbidos in R3 (six better) — having opened with the worst round the latter has ever seen, 115 (cr02).
Jon Baker was nine shots better than his last visit to Royal Óbidos with an 89 in R1; Williams knocked three off his Óbidos best with a 97 in R3 but was seven worse than TEG 7 at Praia D'El Rey.
Neumann shaved one shot off his Óbidos best (98 in R3) yet was 14 shots worse than his last visit to Praia D'El Rey, where he had gone round in 84 in TEG 7.
Patterson had never seen either course before R1 — first visit to Royal Óbidos, first visit to Praia D'El Rey.
decisive_moments: Trophy: R4 holes 15-17 at Praia D'El Rey — level with Patterson walking off the 14th (b23), Alex Baker went 8-7-7 and bled 11 shots (b45), and Patterson's 47 turned a shared lead into a record 168 and a 6-point win (b01).
Green Jacket: R1 H18 at Royal Óbidos — Mullin completed a course-record 87 (cr01) to take the outright Gross lead, and was never headed across the remaining 54 holes on the way to +67 (b02).

Wooden Spoon: R1 H15 at Royal Óbidos — Neumann's quintuple-bogey 8 at the par-3 15th, mid-bleed of 16 shots from the 14th (b44, b29), dropped him last outright and he stayed there for all four rounds (b22).

vehicle_fit_response.note: Taken up, but relocated: the redemption that matters is Alex Baker's (course-worst 115 in R1 to level for the lead in R4 via two personal-best rounds), not the birdie-recovery beats the scorer flagged — and it sits under the bigger frame, a debutant with no TEG record winning the Trophy with the highest score ever posted.
